content.value_statement: React teams need predictable global state without unclear store structure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create typed Zustand stores with selectors and middleware.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of TypeScript Zustand stores for React projects.
Shows subscribeWithSelector middleware as the default store pattern.
Separates store state, actions, and combined store types.
Recommends individual selectors to reduce React rerenders.
Shows how to subscribe to selected store values outside React.
Lists integration steps for store creation, exports, and tests.
limitations: The referenced assets/template.ts file is not included in this package.
It does not generate project-specific business logic without user requirements.
It does not cover persistence, devtools, or server synchronization patterns.
It assumes React, TypeScript, and Zustand are already available.

use_cases.title: Create a Feature Store
use_cases.description: Build a typed Zustand store for feature data, loading state, and actions.

use_cases.title: Standardize Store Patterns
use_cases.description: Apply consistent state, action, selector, and export conventions across a React codebase.

use_cases.title: Review State Usage
use_cases.description: Identify broad subscriptions and replace them with selectors that limit rerenders.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Store
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new feature store.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript Zustand store for [feature name]. Include state fields, action names, and individual selectors for React components.

prompt_templates.title: Add Middleware and Types
prompt_templates.scenario: Add the recommended store structure to an existing idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Zustand store for [domain]. Use subscribeWithSelector, separate state and actions, and explain the exported store type.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Existing State
prompt_templates.scenario: Move component state into a shared store.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this React state design into a typed Zustand store. Preserve behavior, split state from actions, and avoid broad subscriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan External Subscriptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an outside-React subscription flow for this Zustand store. Subscribe to only the needed value and describe cleanup responsibilities.

output_examples.input: Request a store for project items with loading state and add item behavior.
output_examples.output: A structured store plan with typed state, typed actions, selector recommendations, and integration notes for exports and tests.

output_examples.input: Ask how to avoid rerenders when reading items from a Zustand store.
output_examples.output: Guidance to select only the needed state value, avoid whole-store destructuring, and keep component subscriptions narrow.

output_examples.input: Ask for a subscription outside React when a selected identifier changes.
output_examples.output: A subscription approach that watches the selected identifier and runs a focused callback when that value changes.

best_practices: Define state and actions separately before combining them into the store type.
Use selectors for each component instead of reading the entire store.
Add tests for store actions and exported integration points.
anti_patterns: Do not subscribe components to the whole store when they need one value.
Do not mix unrelated feature domains into one broad store.
Do not skip TypeScript interfaces for state and actions.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create typed Zustand stores for React applications.

faq.question: Does it require Zustand knowledge?
faq.answer: Basic React and TypeScript knowledge helps, but the prompts guide the store structure.

faq.question: Why use subscribeWithSelector?
faq.answer: It supports focused subscriptions and helps keep updates limited to selected state.

faq.question: Can it refactor an existing store?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current store shape and desired behavior for a focused refactor.

faq.question: Does it include a template file?
faq.answer: No. The skill mentions a template path, but this package only includes SKILL.md.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
